topic.label: Robotics
topic.desc: Robotics: kinematics and dynamics, perception, motion planning and navigation, control, manipulation, robot software (ROS), simulation, and safety and human-robot interaction. Ontology: Robotics is its own topic; Drones are aerial robots, and Mapping holds SLAM, which robots use for navigation.

concepts: Robot geometry and motion: joints, frames, Jacobians and equations of motion.
Sensing and estimating the world: sensor fusion, detection and pose estimation.
Finding collision-free paths and trajectories and navigating to goals.
Feedback control of robot joints and vehicles: PID, state-space and model-predictive control.
Picking, placing and handling objects with arms and grippers.
Robot middleware: nodes, topics, services, actions and bridges to AI models.
Physics simulation of robots and the gap between simulation and reality.
Safe operation near people, safety cases and interaction design.
skills: Computes end-effector pose from joint angles and the reverse, and reports singularities and multiple solutions.
Builds equations of motion with Lagrangian or Newton-Euler methods and identifies inertial parameters.
Fuses IMU, wheel, camera and LiDAR data with Kalman-type filters and reports the estimate's uncertainty.
Detects objects and estimates their six-degree-of-freedom pose for grasping or avoidance and reports failure cases.
Builds depth maps and point clouds from stereo, time-of-flight or LiDAR sensors and filters noise.
Plans collision-free paths with graph search and sampling-based planners and compares their completeness and cost.
Turns a path into a smooth, time-parameterized trajectory within velocity, acceleration and torque limits.
Configures localization, costmaps and a local planner for a mobile robot and tests recovery behaviours.
Tunes PID gains from step responses and reports overshoot, settling time and stability margin.
Designs LQR or model-predictive controllers from a linear model and checks constraint handling.
Selects motors, drivers and gearing for torque, speed and duty cycle and checks thermal limits.
Plans grasps from object shape and gripper geometry and ranks them by stability and reachability.
Chooses a gripper type for the objects and forces involved and lists payload and compliance limits.
Writes ROS nodes with topics, services and actions and tests message types and timing.
Connects an AI model to a ROS robot through a bridge, restricts which topics and services it may use and keeps a human stop in the loop.
Debugs launch files, parameters and transforms and explains why a node does not start or communicate.
Builds a physics simulation of a robot and its world with sensor models and repeatable test scenarios.
Compares simulated and real robot behaviour and lists the parameters that explain the gap.
Drafts a hazard analysis and safety argument for a robot cell or mobile robot and lists which standards a qualified assessor must check.
Designs how a robot signals intent and responds to people nearby, with speed and separation rules.
